title: Spiritualism wave: seances as common as church

tellings.quote: of these articles in particular said that it was it was as common at the at the height of this thing for an American to get up on a Sunday morning and go to a seance as it was to go to church.

plain: In the 1800s and early 1900s, a craze for spiritualism, the belief that the living can talk with the dead, swept America and Europe, and at its height going to a seance, a gathering to contact spirits, was said to be as common on a Sunday morning as going to church. The filmmaker Tim Alberino tells it from newspaper and magazine articles of that time he came across while working on a project called Birthright, without naming them. He tells it to show how widespread contact with unseen beings once seemed to ordinary people.
